---
title: Meet per-speaker operations
description: How an operator settles a per-speaker transcript chunk that was dispatched to the provider but never answered.
updatedAt: "2026-11-24"
audience: developers
---

Per-speaker transcription (`self_v1`) reserves each chunk's maximum cost on
its session before the provider is called, and settles the reservation once
the outcome is known. The product rules are on
[Per-speaker meeting transcription](/platform/features/meet-per-speaker-transcription).

## Dispatched chunk that never settled

The Meet Worker settles every chunk itself: `released` for a failure before
dispatch, `discarded` or `completed` with the measured cost after the provider
answers, and `unknown` when the provider call fails after dispatch. A Worker
that is stopped or evicted during the provider call can leave a chunk with its
reservation still open. Such a chunk keeps holding its reservation against the
session's `cost_cap_usd` and never shows text.

### Find them

Read-only, with the service role:

```sql
select c.id, c.session_id, c.account_id, c.attempt_started_at, c.reserved_cost_usd
from public.meet_ai_chunks c
where c.stream_id is not null
  and c.status = 'processing'
  and c.reservation_state = 'reserved'
  and c.dispatch_consent_revision is not null
  and c.attempt_started_at < now() - interval '5 minutes';
```

`dispatch_consent_revision is not null` means `mark_dispatch` ran, so the
provider may have been called and billed. A chunk with a null dispatch
revision never reached the provider and is not part of this procedure.

### Settle as `unknown`

Settle each chunk found above as `unknown`. This is a production database
write: it follows the production write approval rules, like any other.

```sql
select private.meet_ai_self_v1_settle_chunk('<chunk id>', 'unknown', null, null, null);
```

- `unknown` moves the chunk's full reservation into the session's
  `cost_unknown_usd`, where it keeps counting against the cost cap. Unknown
  cost is never released.
- The call is idempotent: settling the same chunk as `unknown` again returns
  the row unchanged. Any other outcome after settlement is refused (`55000`).
- Never use `released` (the database refuses it after dispatch) and never use
  `completed` or `discarded` (both need a measured provider cost, and
  `completed` also needs the speaker's current consent).

### What else to expect

- The chunk shows as failed and keeps no text. A resend of the same chunk id
  returns the failed chunk without another provider call.
- The central AI run that was opened for the attempt stays pending until its
  reservation expires (30 minutes); no credits are charged for it. The
  uploader's own credits are never involved.
- Once settled, the post-call review route counts the chunk in
  `unpricedRequests` for the host.
